This is a strong [b]"Yes, but.."[/b] game for me.

The biggest problem with Chained Echoes is that it takes on more than it can chew. Everything is unfocused and scatterbrained. This applies to everything the game offers -- the characters, the story, the length, the areas, the mechanics. There's too much going on. 

I appreciate that there's a whole evocative world underlying the story that's being told, but it's too much to take on too quickly and leads to Proper Noun fatigue within the first hour.

There are a lot of really smart gameplay choices in this game, but the best ideas are smothered by the volume of sub-par or average ideas. Chained Echoes seemingly aspires to be a "grindless" RPG, but there are so many fiddley grinding mechanisms to make your characters superpowered. Equip inefficient skills to level them up for future niche needs. Run around collecting randomly generated cr

Biggest cons are -
1. The sky armor fights are terrible. Wish they didn't exist.
2. Navigating the crystals, combining, removing etc. is a huge pain in the ass.
3. Finding certain paths, areas to climb or jump over is sometimes extremely difficult.
4. Side quests are oddly placed.

Besides those 4, the game is still a really engaging story and a great successor to fans of Chrono Trigger. You can clearly see the inspiration from games like CT, FF9, FF7 and others in the game.

I started Chained Echoes but nearly uninstalled it within the first hour or two. Luckily, I persevered, and I’m glad I stuck with it.

The Good:
	∙	The characters are superb and fun to follow through their adventures
	∙	The story is really great overall (but had some stretches here and there)

	∙	Some textures are difficult to read—it’s hard to tell where to climb up/down, traverse, etc.
	∙	Mixed feelings about the Sky Armors, but that’s just my taste; I’ve never been a fan of mechs

Overall, a really great game with some weakne

Chained Echoes practically screams 16-bit JRPG nostalgia. Be it in the form of graphics or all the included easter eggs. But let's put nostalgia aside ...

The main characters are well-developed, with interesting backgrounds. Their core group narrative is compelling and easy to invest in. This isn't true for all 12 playable characters, though; while the primary heroes shine, the sheer size of the cast means that some party members sadly lack the necessary depth to feel truly essential. Similarly, some antagonists are excellent while others fall short, creating a slightly uneven quality in the overall dramatic tension.

Regarding the story, I will only share that it is rightfully praised in general. In my case, I even respect and "enjoyed" the ending, which seems to have upset many others. To me, it simply made sense; it suited the characters involved.

The offered game mechanics and syst

Chrono Trigger, Final Fantasy, Expedition 33, and dare I say even some modern Persona, all wrapped into a neat 16-bit JRPG style game with a great cast of characters, intriguing story, and superb combat system with a wide variety of mechanics to always keep things fresh. Nothing here feels repetitive or derivative. Sure, it's taken some inspiration but it's largely original, from the art-style to the music. I can't really fault anything so far. The lore is extensive too. I think the only time I was really invested in lore like this was with Funger, although this is not as deep or speculative. It's so wild everything flows so well. Whole teams with millions of dollars can't do this. How did one guy and his contributors manage? Blew threw Act I in three days and it's already cracked my top 15 list. This was made with so much heart and you can tell. Don't hesitate to try this out, honest.

Chained Echoes is the kind of game that feels like it came straight out of my dreams: a 90s-style pixel-art JRPG that pays homage to genre classics such as Final Fantasy VI, Chrono Trigger, Suikoden, and many others.

Developed by a single developer over roughly seven years, Chained Echoes is the quintessential Japanese-style RPG—a genuine love letter to the genre.

What the developer understood perfectly is the difference between honoring the past and preserving its ashes. Many of the most tedious and grindy mechanics of classic JRPGs are simply not here. Progression is closely tied to completing quests and defeating bosses, so forget about spending hours grinding by slaughtering random mobs just to gain a few levels.

The Overdrive system is also a great idea, keeping battles moving at a good pace while adding an interesting layer of strategy.

The only real flaw, IMHO, is the

This game, to me, is a jewel of an RPG, and up there in the list of my most beloved RPG games.

Is a 2d cartoon JRPG-ish game, combat is turn-based and is heavily story-driven. No random encounters, enemies are engaged on place without a separate combat scene (if you're familiar with Chrono Trigger, is pretty similar).

I'm a systems-oriented guy, the combat is fun and well balanced until you look too deep into it, thing 99% of people won't do, there's huge quality of life everywhere, you don't need to grind for levels, but you will need to grind at times for skill levels instead.

The story is very well-paced, characters are likable, there's some kind of wandering and disconnect at the beginning, but everything holds up together shortly after. You'll discover more and more interesting things about the world, the political intrigue and the character's backgrounds as you go on, and there

There is a magic that happens when someone loves an era of gaming so much that they want to commemorate it and pen their own love letter to the feelings they experienced back when they first played these games. Chained Echoes is one such love letter.

It doesn't matter what era of gamer you are, the games you played when you were young and free of responsibilities and burdens (or at least had far fewer of them to deal with) will always hold a special place in your heart.

The feeling I got from the first day I started playing Chained Echoes, to the feelings I'm experiencing now, having rolled credits and completed all achievements just an hour ago are essentially a tribute to what the creators of this game almost certainly intended: Capturing the nostalgia and feeling of that era without being a copycat of the games that inspired it.

If this had been a snes game back in the day, it would today be considered one of the great classics of the era.

The world isn't black and white but moral constants should still remain reasonable. In the end, I hope the dev makes more games. And I hope they bring in additional writers to help course correct some of these issues.

I really tried to get into Chained Echoes, but after about three hours (right after the flaming mantis boss), I just couldn’t keep going. The art style didn’t grab me, the combat feels clunky and lacks feedback, and the Overdrive system is more stressful than fun, constantly having to track which moves raise or lower the gauge kills the flow.

I respect that this was mostly made by one person, but 30 years after games like Chrono Trigger, this just doesn’t feel as enjoyable or rewarding. The writing and pacing didn’t hook me either, and knowing the ending is divisive didn’t help. Overall, it’s not a bad game, but it’s definitely not for me. Uninstalled and moving on.

I came into this game with high hopes and in a lot of areas the game delivered.  There's a very robust customization system, beautiful pixel graphics, and a passable story, if a little scattered toward the end.

Unfortunately the game chose to include the presence of same-sex relationships.  While these are not as glaringly prevalent as some other modern entries in this genre, it could have done without them, and I found myself more and more annoyed as I approached endgame, to the point where I just decided to cut my experience short by finishing the game.  I think the most annoying part is without those beats the game had such promise, like a good meal ruined by an unpleasant aftertaste.

It has beautiful art style and interesting additions to the mechanisms and grind of turn based rpgs, however, the story is just way too boring and getting through it feels like a slog. Believe me, can look at my hours and see how I've tried.

Unfortunately, I just did not enjoy the hours I invested in the game.

While Chained Echoes can be a lot of fun, there are a fair few things holding it back. 

1. The upgrading system feels kind bad when you're getting new gear fairly quickly and not being able to easily swap over your crystals.
2. Crystal farming can be such a pain if you don't have a fair amount of time to dedicate to it. 
3. The story has so many twists and turns, but it gets kind of annoying after a while. To the point where anyone with a portrait isn't to be trusted.
4. The overheat mechanic is kind of annoying when you're starting to get into a flow state.
5. The lack of traditional levels makes progress feel weird. 

It's a fairly fun game if you can look past those and use status effects on bosses. Not a game I would be playing again. ♥

My biggest complaint would be the writing. This game could have greatly benefited from an editor. There's a lot of immature language and humor throughout the somewhat limited exposition. I'll end up finishing it but I don't expect this to be something I'll revisit any time soon.

This game is actually interesting from a story perspective, but somehow it feels like something is missing and it becomes boring. Maybe it's the level grinding that doesn't matter, because what matters is grinding skill points. Furthermore, the grinding is very boring because there is no Auto Battle (you have to stare at the monitor without rest just to level up), and the enemies here are very difficult. I understand that it's to get the adrenaline pumping and sharpen the brain. But I play this game to relax and listen to the story. Not everyone has the same opinion. At least for grinding, there should be easier enemies. For the second drawback, there is no AUTO NEXT in the dialogue. In 2025, this feature is actually very useful. As for the gameplay technique, it's fine.
